title: Elastic, inelastic and sticking collision energy
prereq: P01 momentum, P03 isolated collision, PH01 signed velocity, kinetic energy.
goals: Write momentum and kinetic-energy ledgers separately.
Calculate the sticking collision's common speed and energy conversion.
Recognise that ideal elasticity supplies an additional constraint beyond momentum.

sections.heading: Momentum does not guarantee kinetic-energy conservation
sections.body: In a brief collision with negligible net external impulse, system momentum is conserved. But collision deformation and heat can reduce translational kinetic energy. A sticking collision is perfectly inelastic: the bodies share one velocity, even though some initial kinetic energy becomes other forms.

sections.heading: Find the speed from momentum, not energy
sections.body: For two constant masses that latch, common velocity V = (m_A u_A + m_B u_B)/(m_A+m_B). The numerator is the signed momentum sum. Then compute K_before = ½m_A u_A² + ½m_B u_B² and K_after = ½(m_A+m_B)V². Only when external work during contact is negligible is their difference an internal energy-conversion witness.

sections.heading: An ideal elastic collision is a different model
sections.body: An ideal elastic collision conserves total translational K as well as total momentum. In one dimension, separation speed equals approach speed for a central elastic collision. Two bodies generally leave with different velocities and may rebound; using a common velocity would impose sticking, not elasticity.

sections.heading: Restitution supplies missing information
sections.body: If only total momentum is known, there are normally two unknown outgoing speeds but one equation. A specified one-dimensional restitution coefficient e supplies a second relation: v_B − v_A = e(u_A − u_B) for A approaching B. Typical passive collisions use 0 ≤ e ≤ 1; confirm line-of-impact and relative approach assumptions.

worked.name: Foundation · sticking energy loss
worked.setup: A 2 kg cart moving +3 m/s sticks to a stationary 1 kg cart.
steps: P_initial=2×3=+6 kg·m/s, joined mass 3 kg, V=+2 m/s.
worked.check: Total momentum is unchanged; kinetic energy falls by 3 J.

worked.name: Connected · identical elastic pucks
worked.setup: A 1 kg puck at +4 m/s strikes resting 1 kg puck centrally and elastically.
steps: For equal masses, ideal one-dimensional elastic impact swaps velocities.
Both P=+4 kg·m/s and K=8 J before/after.
worked.check: This swap is NOT a universal rule for inelastic or unequal-mass impacts.

worked.name: Transfer · partial restitution
worked.setup: A 2 kg body at +3 m/s strikes stationary 1 kg body with e=0.5.
steps: K_initial=9 J, K_final=2.25+4.5=6.75 J; loss=2.25 J.
worked.check: Momentum conservation alone did not give both individual final speeds.

trap.wrong: Assume total kinetic energy remains unchanged because momentum is conserved.
trap.repair: Name the contact type; compute outgoing velocities using momentum plus the contact law, then check energy separately.

assumptions: Only short contact intervals have negligible external impulse.
The elastic condition is an additional premise, not a derived consequence of momentum.
Restitution is defined along a given line of impact; these models are extension-review.

model.label: Teaching model: incoming speed for 2 kg cart sticking to 3 kg at rest

prompt.stem: A 1 kg cart moving RIGHT at +4 m/s strikes a resting 3 kg cart on a smooth rail. They STICK in a brief contact with negligible external horizontal impulse. Find the common velocity, the energy converted during contact, and conserved total momentum.
prompt.prediction: Predict whether the joined pair is slower and whether its kinetic energy equals the initial kinetic energy.
prompt.boundaryPrompt: Changed law: with the SAME 1 kg at +4 and 3 kg at rest, the collision is ideal 1D ELASTIC, not sticking. Find both final velocities and the kinetic energy lost.
